title: First jazz solos with Wynn and Teddy Rowe's half-cocked mute
summary: His first jazz solos came with Albert Wynn on sax, and Teddy Rowe taught him half-cocking the mute.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: Course, as I said, I wouldn't call that jazz. I didn't get into to solo jazz playing, I don't think, until let's see. Well Albert Wynn that was when -- I did -- as a saxophone player. I did a lot of solo work with him. And

Jelly Roll Jelly Roll with Teddy Rowe, Teddy Rowe was a great admirer -- he admired me quite a lot but he never got a chance to use me much. He taught me also a lot about solo playing, about half cocking the mute in the bell, now he was the originator of that. He taught me that.
